notes: Source navigation metadata authored without running deletion, registry, architecture or acceptance checks.
Gated identifies a source-visible fresh withDeletionGate callback around the effect, not an observed deletion result or a complete architecture proof.

Deletion admission checks an acknowledged DELETION_ALLOWED ops audit row before the synchronous callback. Audit failure prevents the effect. A denied operation can still have auditPersisted false when its denial audit cannot be written.

Guard-event pruning uses the resolved workspace, the selected DUAL_WRITE or CUTOVER store and a fresh gate. The gate audit is written through appendOpsAuditEvent, not inferred from the void best-effort emitGuardEvent contract.

Direct spill-store removal and purge use broad workspace spill scope because the locator owner does not prove all shared-session references. Lifecycle supplies complete authenticated sessionIds, but its nested direct-store gate can conservatively block unrelated spill holds.

Exempt is limited here to operation-owned unpublished atomic-write staging files and exclusive control-lock coordination cleanup. Other apparent temporary, rollback, quarantine, socket and verification-workspace deletions remain deferred until their ownership and publication boundaries are established.
Deferred is not an exemption. Out-of-slice routes must be resolved before full deletion coverage can be claimed; protected ledger, A4, approval, API and Studio code was not changed.

Rows include sync filesystem source occurrences, namespace and literal-require bindings, literal or template SQLite DELETE text, followed indirect erasure calls and the public payload-erasure definition. Several rows trace the same physical effect, so row totals are not counts of distinct deleted resources.

Line numbers and source excerpts are navigation hints that may move. This inventory does not close computed aliases or SQL, asynchronous filesystem calls, rename-based replacement, schema cascades, external subprocess deletions or third-party storage APIs.
